stemMarkdown: If 18 men working 9 hours a day complete a job in 15 days, how many days will 24 men working 6 hours a day take to complete the same job? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The job is $18 \times 15 \times 9 = 2430$ man-hours. The new team supplies $24 \times 6 = 144$ man-hours per day, so it takes $\dfrac{2430}{144} = 16.875$ days.
altSolutionMarkdown: Chain rule in one line: $\dfrac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \dfrac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$. Everything that supplies effort multiplies on top; the work done divides underneath.
